name: optimistic-locking-version-p3
prompt: how do I stop two concurrent edits from silently overwriting each other when saving the same record

chunks.content: switched the dashboard to a dark theme using CSS custom properties
added a 50-connection database pool with a health-check ping on checkout
the nightly batch grabs a Postgres advisory lock so two cron hosts cannot run the same report job concurrently
export request latency histograms to Prometheus on /metrics
outbound email is pushed onto a background queue and sent by a worker
cache the product catalog for 10 minutes and bust it on any write
resolved a merge conflict where two branches edited the same config file and combined both concurrent changes by hand
switch the list endpoint to keyset pagination using the last seen id
record every admin action in an append-only audit log
enabled gzip compression on responses larger than 1 KB
decided to add a version number column and only commit an update when the row's current version still matches the one the editor read, so a stale save is rejected instead of clobbering a newer change
when the compare-and-set update affects zero rows we surface a conflict to the client and ask them to reload and reapply their edit, so neither concurrent writer's change is silently lost
the API requires an If-Match header carrying the record's last known version, and returns 412 when the stored version has moved on, preventing a lost update from a second simultaneous edit
store all timestamps in UTC and convert in the UI
the /healthz endpoint returns 200 once the database pool is ready
